message.content:
**London’s time zone**

| Period | Standard abbreviation | Offset from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) |
|--------|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| **Winter / Non‑DST period** | `GMT` – Greenwich Mean Time | UTC ± 00:00 |
| **Summer / Daylight Saving Time** | `BST` – British Summer Time | UTC ± 01:00 |

* In practice, London follows **British Summer Time (BST)** between the last Sunday of March and the last Sunday of October, when clocks move forward one hour (UTC + 1).  
* Outside those dates it reverts to **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)**, i.e., UTC + 0.

So if you’re looking at an exact timestamp:

```
• Jan–Mar & Oct–Dec → GMT (UTC+0)
• Apr–Sep            → BST (UTC+1)
```
